Luckily the care for scorpions and whip scorpions is fairly similar to tarantulas. The main difference (with Emperor Scorpions) is that they generally need a heat source and very high humidity.

Do your research for sure - Every species is different and I cannot possibly list out everything you'd need to know in a comment without a specific species. This is a really nice "general" care sheet that I like to refer people towards when they're looking for information on tarantulas that has some of the costs listed out. A lot of this information would apply to just about any arachnid so I highly suggest you check it out during your research.

In general the costs associated with keeping arachnids is actually very low. A regular fish tank or kritter keeper will do just fine as long as you use the appropriate size and make sure to have a glass or metal lid - preferably with locks or latches to secure it.

Health/safety wise you're obviously responsible for not only your own but for the arachnid's as well. With an emperor or whip scorpion you're not really in a whole lot of danger because they can only really do so much "damage" but it wouldn't be a pleasant experience for either of you should something go wrong. It's actually much more likely that the arachnid would be injured before you would. Do your research and keep a healthy respect for whatever you end up getting regardless of how "dangerous" it is.
